speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Chairman, I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head T of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Sir, as we continue to strive to make Singapore a more inclusive and liveable city, it is crucial that our policies evolve to meet the new trends and needs of all Singaporeans through different generations.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Today, I wish to highlight a few observations in housing options and offer suggestions for consideration.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: First, Housing and Development Board (HDB) Build-To-Order (BTO) flats for middle-income households and singles.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The younger generation are now settling down much later and many begin to purchase their first home closer to or after the age of 30.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: For these couples, they usually find that they are left out of a prized opportunity to purchase their first BTO flat from the Government which can form a part of their nest-egg for retirement.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Some even do not qualify for the direct purchase of executive condominiums and have no choice but to purchase a resale flat or a private property.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Depending on the age of the resale flat and its location, it results in some inherent restrictions to the buyer, for example, the loan amount available, inability to access HDB concessionary housing loan and others.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Similarly, we are seeing a growing trend of more singles within our community.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: In today's market and for those who are 35 years old and above, there are many whose income would exceed this threshold and be disqualified to purchase BTO flat, not to mention that some singles are still facing difficulties in being allocated a flat in the regular BTO or Sale of Balance Flats exercise.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Further, despite having been given the option to purchase all flat types, there are singles who are still unable to buy BTO flat and have to settle for a resale flat.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Many of them wish to be living near their parents or siblings to provide caregiving and support as they age.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: But these resale flats are typically in mature estates, and singles face the same issues as that of the middle-income couples.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Based on a single income, it is even harder for singles to consider purchasing a private property.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Also, what viable options can be made available for these groups within the decade?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: While there are Singaporeans who aspire to progress from public into private housing, this is not a default choice for many young couples and singles who wish to have the option of living in public housing purchased from the Government.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I acknowledge that the Government has continuously adjusted policies to cater for different population segments to ensure their basic housing needs are addressed.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I hope more can be done for these specific groups so that they could also enjoy the benefits of our nation's progress and not be caught by the affordability gap to own a home within their means.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I have made these requests before based on my residents' feedback.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: We are encouraging our seniors to age in place.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Depending on the needs and mobility of the seniors, the cost of modifications can be prohibitive.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: At times, individual homeowners may not be able to secure contractors who are willing to take up what we call the "small" jobs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: A home that is not equipped to support the seniors' needs can become a significant hindrance to their well-being.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Small but essential modifications, such as grab bars, non-slip flooring and ramps, can greatly improve their quality of life.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: By extending support to seniors in private property, we send a strong message that every senior matters; regardless of where they stay.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Even if the scope of support is smaller than the public housing, providing some level of assistance to these seniors would ease their financial burden and improve their quality of life.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Our population is ageing and we must take proactive steps to ensure our elderly citizens can live with dignity and comfort.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Third, housing option for families with special needs children or adults.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: In 2024 Ministry of National Development's (MND's) Committee of Supply (COS), I spoke up for divorcees with special needs children and asked whether interim housing can be provided for these divorcees or those that are still in the process of finalising their divorce.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I wish to raise this point again, but more on the perspective of long-term housing for any family with special needs children or adults.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: For these adults, I refer to those who are diagnosed with special needs or disabilities since young and are now in their adulthood.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Personally, I have encountered families with such situations and some of whom are my residents.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: These families often struggle to find an HDB flat that meet their unique requirements.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: In some cases, they need to relocate due to the difficulties in the current or former neighbourhoods that they lived in.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: It is disheartening to hear of families facing hostility from neighbours who may not fully understand or be willing to accommodate the challenges of caring for special needs children or adults.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Noise disturbance being a common issue for dispute.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: To cite another recent example of a resident living in private property with a remaining lease of less than 10 years.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: One is a retiree and the other a housewife, they do not have active income nor huge savings and will unlikely make much profit from the sale of their private property given its running out lease.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The reason for them wanting a larger flat is solely because their son can only move around on a wheelchair and, with other medical conditions, he requires the space; especially, they have a live-in helper since the elderly couple cannot physically manage their son independently.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Moving multiple times between flats is not ideal for them for the reasons stated.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: They are also worried whether they are able to find an affordable interim place to rent and whether the landlord is willing to accept them, given their son's condition.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: This couple's only hope is for the HDB flat to be a more permanent home for their son and is certainly not expecting to purchase it for windfall proceeds from a future sale.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I fully appreciate there are many requests and families with varying conditions in Singapore.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Caring for one with special needs requires extensive resources, patience and a conducive environment.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Unfortunately, when these families faced unkindness or intolerance from neighbours, it places even more stress on the caregiver.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Apart from individual housing needs, we must, over time, address the topic of social cohesion between private and public housing.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Forward Singapore is fundamentally about community building and we should ensure that our urban planning reflects this vision by fostering greater neighbourliness and mutual understanding.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Shared facilities are just one means towards this, but the interaction of people from diverse backgrounds and housing types are more critical in enhancing community bonding.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The need for social cohesion is even more pressing in today's society, where income disparity, housing segregation and other factors can inadvertently lead to division.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: We should not allow a housing type to define social circles or create barriers.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: By designing common spaces that are welcoming to all, we can cultivate a shared identity and strengthen our social fabric.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Let us work together to ensure that our housing policies and urban planning align with the evolving needs of our citizens.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: As Singaporeans know, resale flat prices can be very high.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Even flats with 60 years left on their lease can cost well in excess of half a million dollars.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: A significant number of resale flats are purchased by first-time married couples who must devote a significant chunk of their Central Provident Fund (CPF) retirement funds on servicing mortgage payments.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: By the time retirement comes along, they may have to downgrade to unlock the equity in their HDB flat, equity which is likely to have depleted significantly because of the reality of the 99-year lease decay countdown.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: With the days of iron rice bowls, lifetime job security and pensions no longer the norm for Singaporeans, retirement adequacy for the current and later generations is a more significant issue today.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Another reality is that current generations of Singaporeans will not ride the same property escalator as their parents did, from which many ascended from public housing to private homes and, in some cases, to buying a landed property within a single lifetime.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: More pertinently, when compared to their peers who purchase a new BTO flat to live in, those who buy an older resale flat, say, with 60 years left on the lease, all other things being equal, will have less money to buy a smaller flat when they retire and, by extension, will have less for their CPF life payouts as well.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: We need to see how we can strengthen the retirement adequacy of resale flat buyers who buy flats with a significant chunk of their leases already expended.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: A renewed focus on building the retirement incomes of first-time resale flat buyers would ensure that resale flat buyers consider their resale flat purchases carefully, with an eye on the 99-year lease countdown clock and their retirement planning considerations in mind.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The HDB Home Ownership Scheme, which allowed the use of CPF money in 1968 and the sale of HDB flats on the resale market in 1971, have become an increasingly significant factor when it comes to retirement adequacy.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The objective of home ownership in and of itself is not the problem.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: However, with the 99-year lease decay looming over Singaporeans and far more foreseeable than it was from the vantage point of 1968 and 1971, the fundamental objective of CPF for retirement needs must come back into focus.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: For the immediate term and given how complex HDB housing policy has become, any changes and alternatives with respect to HDB policy will have to be explored at the margins.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: To this end, I would suggest there could be some policy space to better protect first-time buyers of older resale HDB properties from the reality of the 99-year lease decay countdown clock.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In the face of disruptions brought on by COVID-19, the Government has made what I would describe as a breathtaking range of moves on housing in the last few years and achieved a very strong report card.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Now I know supply-side measures by the Government will need more time to work themselves into the HDB resale market and, eventually, the market will stabilise.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But there is also something to be said about the fairness to whole cohorts of home buyers, especially first timers, when they are caught in a prolonged upturn in the HDB resale market cycle and are either priced out completely from the resale market or are pressured into a buying decision in order to lock-in a price, despite a preference to look around a bit more in the market.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And the more time it takes for measures to cool the resale market, the greater the number of cohorts affected as such.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I wonder if this is fair, especially for first-timers.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I hope the Government can develop more policy options on the demand side, to cool the HDB resale market more quickly, when needed.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The public housing market has always been regulated separately, with its own rules and design to achieve key social goals.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: So, it stands to reason that the HDB market should have its own buyer stamp duty framework that is decoupled from the quanta and dynamics of private property transactions.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: This separate buyer stamp duty framework for the HDB market can give the Government greater policy optionality when it needs to quickly cool the resale market, to preserve fairness for all cohorts of home buyers.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Chairman, in recent years, the Government has enhanced the Public Rental Scheme by introducing new typologies to provide more housing options for lower-income households, such as the Single Room Shared Facilities pilot.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Could MND provide an update on the pilot, and how the Government is continuing to improve the Public Rental Scheme to better support the evolving needs of our vulnerable groups?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Henry Kwek, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Chairman, to meet the growing demand for homes, driven by smaller family size and evolving housing needs, MND has significantly ramped up the supply of BTOs and private homes.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: These efforts are paying off, with supply and demand now stabilizing at pre-COVID-19 levels, giving home buyers more options.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: At the same time, strong income growth since the pandemic has shifted housing needs and many young couples are taking longer to settle down, whether due to career priorities, financial planning or lifestyle choices.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: However, some aspiring homeowners, particularly Singaporeans who do well in their career but lack familial support for down payments for private property, face challenges in securing affordable housing.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: That would provide more housing options for the upper middle-income segments, ensuring that Singapore remains a place where home ownership is accessible, aspirations are met and the ladder of social mobility remains strong for future generations.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: The cost of living, especially the price of cooked food, remain one of the top concerns for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Rising food prices driven by inflation and global supply disruptions have placed pressure on households, especially lower-income families and seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: At the same time, it is also important to allow food businesses the flexibility to adapt, innovate and to cater to diverse consumer preference.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Therefore, the budget meal initiative strikes this balance, offering lower-cost meal options for price-sensitive consumers, on the one hand, while ensuring that hawkers and eateries are not restricted in their offerings.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This approach also helps to maintain a vibrant food culture while supporting those who need it the most.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Since the launch of the budget meal initiative, can MND share what has been the take-up rate so far, and what more can we do to further expand affordable food options in our neighbourhood?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Chairman, the Ministry and HDB announced the Budget Meal initiative in March 2023 to provide Singaporeans with more affordable food options.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Under this initiative, all HDB coffee shops that are renewing their tenancies from May 2023 will be required to offer at least four budget meals and two budget drink options.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are we on track to have all of the coffee shops leased from HDB offering budget meals?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In a number of older HDB estates, many coffee shops there are bought and sold in the open market, and not leased from HDB.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Hence, MND will need to work with the private operators to come onboard the Budget Meal initiative.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So far, how many and what is the proportion of privately-owned coffee shops have joined the scheme?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What has been the feedback on its usefulness so far?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For senior citizens who have difficulty going online, how does the Ministry share with them updated information on where to go for budget meals?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: CIPC projects cover basic infrastructure, recreational facilities and communal amenities, including playgrounds, fitness areas and linkways.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: For example, on multiple occasions in this House, I have asked about the quantum of CIPC funds given to each Town Council, so there is a clear quantifiable data point to indicate how much taxpayer money has been given to each Town Council.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In 2017, the then Minister for National Development said that MND did not prescribe any standardised way for Town Councils to present the CIPC quantum.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: When I asked the same substantive question last year, the Minister replied that the amount of CIPC funding disbursed to each Town Council each year is based on the works completed by the Town Council as the implementing agent.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The disbursement is reported in the respective Town Council's annual financial statements.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The annual disbursement to the Town Councils includes CIPC projects approved over multiple years, as projects may take years and exclude CIPC projects implemented by the Citizens' Consultative Committees (CCCs).

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Even though the disbursement is reported in the annual financial statements of all Town Councils, without a standardised way of presenting the information, tracking the absolute amount of CIPC funding channelled to each Town Council can be challenging and inaccurate, particularly if one compares the amounts disbursed by MND to PAP and opposition Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Opposition Town Councils need not get the buy-in and support from CCCs that work exclusively with PA grassroots advisors anymore.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In view of the change of approach since 2021, may I ask the Minister to answer these questions relating to all new CIPC proposals from 2021 to date?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Could the Minister please name the top five Town Councils in terms of CIPC funds granted and the quantum extended to each Town Council respectively?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Please also name the bottom five Town Councils and the quantum of CIPC funds granted to each respectively over the same period.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Please include projects regardless of whether they came from the Town Councils directly or through the CCCs.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: How does the Committee decide which project proposals are approved and which are rejected by the CIPC committee?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And finally, in this regard, would MND meet with elected opposition Town Councillors to discuss projects which it rejects?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, I brought up in last year's Budget and COS debate that more can be done for persons with disabilities in the area of housing.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: However, speaking to people on the ground, not everyone is aware they can apply.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: The naming of the scheme suggests that the programme is meant for seniors only.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Alternatively, could MND consider a similar but separate scheme for persons with disabilities?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Those who require home modifications should be fully informed of their options to empower independent living at home.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Under such a scheme, and this is a point I made last year, MND can then widen the list of improvement items that specifically cater to persons with disabilities beyond those with mobility challenges.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have been raising this issue in Parliament every year since 2021.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In the past year, I continued to receive feedback from affected residents on their unhappiness over the lack of same-floor lift access for the remaining five blocks.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The lack of lift access is still a very real issue for some of my affected residents, especially those with mobility needs requiring assistance to access the stairs outside their units when they have to go out, not to mention risks during emergencies.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have said previously that I would feel the pain when residents told me that their parents or grandparents had to be carried when accessing the stairs next to their units.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Residents also have to pay additional charges for delivery items.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I would also like to ask the Government, in the past five years, how many HDB flats without same-floor lift access had been provided with viable mechanical options on the adjoining staircase?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have also heard the Minister's explanation to the other MPs on 18 February this year, and I would again like to call on the Government to not just look at the issue of lift access from the angle of cost alone, something which could have been mitigated or avoided if HDB had tendered out lift upgrading projects consisting of blocks with problematic designs together with other HDB blocks with no design issues for LUP earlier.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Of the remaining affected HDB units without same-floor lift access in Hougang, I hope HDB can provide an update as to which units still face technical constraints beyond the application of costly solutions and which units have not been offered LUP due to high cost alone.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I hope HDB also inform residents in writing.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This may also allow more in-depth study and better understanding on a stack-by-stack basis.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Please also inform residents of the alternative mechanical options available and the cost involved.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Please inform my Town Council so that it can convey HDB's explanation when asked by residents and it can also play a supportive role in the quest for solutions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In closing, I would like to call on the Government to consider giving same-floor lift access to all HDB flats where it is technically not impossible for access to be provided with the LUP, save for reason of cost.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: After all, the design oversight is no fault of the flat owners, and it is a matter of equity for all HDB flat owners.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Back then, climbing the stairs was not an issue.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: But today, as they age, many face mobility challenges and their priorities have shifted.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: What was once a desirable feature has become a source of hardship.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Last month, one of my Nanyang residents, came to see me.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: She is 68 years old and lives in a segmented unit and suffers from weak knees, making stairs a daily struggle.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Her sister-in-law, a stroke patient lives next door, also a segmented unit, faces even greater mobility challenges.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Both wish to apply for a BTO flat with lift access, but as second-time applicants, their chances are slim.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: It is a story shared by many residents living in segmented units across Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: That is why I urge the Minister for National Development to review the policy on segmented units.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: These residents are not asking for special treatment; they are asking for a fair chance to age with dignity and ease.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: To address this issue, I propose the following measures: One, install additional lifts in segmented blocks wherever it is technically possible.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: After buying back the segmented units, HDB should not resell them.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Instead, HDB could collaborate with entities like hospitals to rent out these units to foreign nurses and medical workers, preventing the cycle from repeating.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: These measures would provide a permanent solution, ensuring no Singaporean is left behind as they age.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Let us be decisive, take bold action to resolve this issue once and for all.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Each of these blocks are 17 floors high, with a total of 192 units, served by two lift lobbies in each block.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Chairman, Sir, I look after residents in several private estates in Jalan Besar GRC and wish to speak on their behalf.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I appreciate that all Singaporeans, whether residing in public or private estates, benefit from the Government's efforts in national and civil defence, infrastructure, public transport, education, healthcare and other essential services.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Housing type, of course, often serves as a proxy for resource allocation, especially for lower-income families with limited assets.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Private estate living offers advantages such as higher asset values, greater privacy and renovation flexibility, but it also comes with challenges, including self-management responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How can MND assist elderly residents in private estates to better age in place?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For condominiums managing individual procurements, can MND facilitate sharing best practice in procurements in property management and maintenance?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Could a dedicated agency mediate disputes between residents and Management Councils (MCs) to ensure fair and timely resolutions?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How can the Government incentivise private condos to adopt sustainable practices, such as energy-efficient lighting or water-saving measures?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Lastly, how can MND ensure residents have direct access to updated community news and opportunities to participate in social initiatives for all ages?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These steps would enhance inclusivity and support for private estate residents.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The Urban Redevelopment Authority’s (URA’s) long-term plan review highlights the Government's strategy of building inclusive and close-knit towns by improving connectivity and injecting amenities within neighbourhoods and close to homes.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Unlike older HDB estates or new BTO estates for certain neighbourhoods, all precincts within Sengkang are currently underserved when it comes to the lack of coffee shops and everyday conveniences in the immediate neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Hence, the Sengkang team has been actively exploring opportunities to bring greater F&B and commercial conveniences to our residents.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: For example, we studied the possibility of converting under-utilised spaces, such as unused multi-storey carparks, although I understand that technical limitations have rendered some of these proposals unfeasible.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: During the 2023 COS debate, in response to my call for the MND to address the lack of amenities within Sengkang, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann noted that URA and the relevant agencies are currently reviewing plans to further develop the Sengkang Town Centre.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Therefore, would the MND be able to provide a status update to these plans?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Moreover, with the recent decommissioning of Compassvale Bus Interchange, the site could be used to develop amenities, such as an integrated community development.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The empty plot of land next to Compass One could also be better utilised for a permanent building, rather than merely for the occasional "pasar malam" in the interest of maximising land use while rejuvenating the wider Sengkang neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Specifically for hawker centres, the NEA today manages 121 markets and hawker centres, and after decades of waiting, residents at Buangkok and Anchorvale can finally have their own hawker centre.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I understand from the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment COS earlier that there will be five more hawker centres planned in the future.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: There is strong justification for another hawker centre to serve the needs of residents in the central and eastern regions of Sengkang, especially when the opportunity presents itself today, and especially when we consider that this is not just about the standalone hawker centre, but potentially an integrated development that will enable us to better maximise and achieve the highest and best use for the centrally located plots of land there.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: On improving connectivity, BTO developments, such as Rivervale Shores, include flats targeted at both seniors and families with young children.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Hence, the HDB should proactively work with the Land Transport Authority (LTA) to ensure that the surrounding infrastructure should be made barrier free, and also by retrofitting nearby overhead bridges with lifts ahead of the project's Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP).

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: While there is unlikely to be many more new BTO estates in Sengkang, given limited areas for development, for the benefit of future residents of future BTO estates across Singapore, I hope that this can be included as part of tender requirements for contractors engaged by the HDB for new BTO projects.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This sector is fundamental to Singapore’s long-term urban development, sustainability, and economic resilience and ensuring its continued strength requires strategic transformation.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: With major national projects such as Changi Terminal 5 on the horizon, the success of this initiative is critical in building a resilient and future-ready industry.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Can the Government provide an update on the task force’s progress in supporting the built environment consultancy sector?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Over the years, MND has made tremendous strides in supporting seniors to age-in-place within the HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Additionally, an increased number of Active Aging Centres (AACs) have been set up within HDB estates, providing seniors with space for social engagement, activities and community support.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Moving forward, MND and Town Councils will work together through the Age Well SG programme to retrofit common areas, making public spaces more senior-friendly and accessible for all.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: MPs like myself from PAP Senior Wing certainly welcome these significant moves.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And in general, can MND share its vision for helping Singaporean seniors age-in-place within the private estates?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For seniors living in private estates and who can afford it, ageing-in-place can be achieved through renovations to make their homes more elderly-friendly.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Singapore is well-known internationally as a clean and green city.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, as a "City in Nature", we face the challenge of needing to balance the protection of ecosystems with the safety, cleanliness and comfort of residents.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The increasing number of human-wildlife conflicts is one of the main problems highlighted by my constituents.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I shared in this House two years ago, the problems of crows, mynahs and chickens in my estates.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Today, the growing populations of crows and mynahs continue to disturb my residents.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They are noisy, dirty and aggressive, and attack bewildered passers-by and residents.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Over the years, Bishan-Toa Payoh Town Council has received hundreds of reports and feedback about these birds.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In addition to crow attacks, frequent and longstanding complaints include bird droppings on laundry, windows and ledges, food and rubbish messes created by their scavenging, and noise nuisance.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The bird droppings are hygiene and health concerns.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They affect the general aesthetics of the town and lead to higher maintenance costs.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Town Councils need more assistance, resources and expertise from the National Parks Board (NParks) to remove nests, reduce shelters and food sources for these birds.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We also want to ensure that we are not chasing the flocks to other estates.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Climate change has brought about unpredictable weather patterns, such as the prolonged monsoon in January, and with La Nina expected to bring more wet months this year, are our older public flats, many built in the eighties and nineties, equipped to withstand such conditions?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Many of these flats are experiencing water seepage from roofs and external walls, leading to wet floors and increased fall risk, especially for the elderly.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Other than funding, our experience managing complex water seepage cases has been very frustrating.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: How can HDB better equip resource and incentivise the engineers to achieve better rectification timelines?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Two, to expand spaces for sports and recreation for active seniors?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This is not TikTok but the sound of a rising sport called pickleball.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It is encouraging to see more seniors staying active through sports.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: However, in Nee Soon South, as well as in other constituencies, the demand for courts is rising with badminton, basketball, netball, sepak takraw and now pickleball competing for space.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Our PA colleagues now struggle with juggling court allocations while promoting active lifestyles.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: With the growing momentum of active ageing, more seniors will remain mobile and eager to engage in sports.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: MND must plan ahead to meet this rising demand by repurposing underutilised spaces for recreation.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Currently, some community gardens are located on multi-storey carpark top decks.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: But certain fruit trees are prohibited due to concerns about the root damage to the roofs.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We can relocate these gardens to the green spaces between HDB blocks and convert the multi-storey car park rooftops into sports facilities.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Installing safety netting along the sides and overhead will ensure that ball and record games can be played safely without concerns about errant shots going over parapets.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Three, let us allow and encourage small plot planting in HDB front and backyards.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Many elderly residents cultivate small gardens outside their ground floor units, growing flowers, papayas or banana trees.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: However, currently MND inspections classify these as defects.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Guidelines can be established to ensure proper maintenance and prevent issues such as mosquito breeding.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Additionally, incentives can be introduced to encourage best practices.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I am grateful to the Singapore Land Authority for working with us closely in Nee Soon South to allow green spaces in our estates to be used for permaculture planting.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This effort will benefit from a bigger and louder push from the Government through a national initiative to raise awareness and invite participation by residents.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Imagine weighing in the papayas, pomelos, pumpkins and bitter gourds for the competition, and then distributing the fruits of this labour to friends and neighbours in the vicinity of each community.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It would be a joyous experience for everyone involved.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: One caveat to ensure fairness and adherence to nature principles, we must stipulate that chemical fertilisers are not allowed and assessors must be equipped to detect the violation of these rules.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Studies show that gardening provides significant health benefits, including improved physical activity, reduced stress, enhanced cognitive function, preventing depression, heart disease and dementia.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The vision of little farms everywhere not only supports our food resilience, it also contributes to a healthier and more sustainable Singapore through both the physical activity and the nutritious low carbon produce.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I urge MND to consider and implement these recommendations toward healthier lives in all our estates and neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Joan Pereira, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They are looking forward to the senior-friendly features, such as barrier-free access, rest points, therapeutic gardens and active health fitness trails.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I understand the targeted and systematic approach taken by MND to launch: first, the new EUP for Silver Estates, where there is a higher concentration of seniors; followed by the EUP for Regular Estates later.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, there are currently different types of repairs and upgrades which may need to be done more urgently, regardless of the private estates' locations.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These are the ones which pose safety and health concerns, such as lighting in certain areas, potholes and drain covers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These are to reduce tripping hazards and potential breeding grounds for mosquitoes, for example.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: An increasing number of our HDB blocks are crossing the over 50-year mark.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We need to rejuvenate our older estates so that they remain good homes for our people.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For ageing blocks with widespread, common and recurring problems, I appeal to HDB to consider a review of its approach to such issues.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Two years ago in March, I shared in this House the numerous building problems plaguing my residents at Henderson Crescent estate.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many residents have to deal with water leakages, mould infestation and spalling concrete.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Resident A has difficulty getting the cooperation of the upper floor unit to repair the ceiling leak.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The family is helpless under the leaking water and has to breathe in harmful mould spores every day.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Resident B and her husband managed to get repairs done for their kitchen ceiling leak under the HDB Goodwill Repair Assistance (GRA) scheme.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The leaking problem resurfaced just nine months later in January this year.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Resident C, an elderly stroke patient who lives alone, suffers from a double whammy.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Water leaks into his unit from the flat above and his unit is leaking into the unit below.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: He will have to bear double, the co-sharing repair costs, which are a heavy financial burden on him.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: PA grassroots had offered him financial assistance for repairs, but he did not take them up for personal reasons.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such repairs are especially financially challenging for elderly residents without family support.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many residents in Henderson Crescent have expressed to me their desire for the Selective En bloc Redevelopment Scheme (SERS).

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry share an update on its plans for ageing estates and review the Home Improvement Programme (HIP), SERS and VERS?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Several of my residents have written appeals to object to the rezoning.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They are concerned that their views will be obstructed once the new development is built.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They also worry that there will be more traffic congestion in the area once the neighbouring land is developed.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: After all, a property is one of the most expensive assets which a resident will buy in their lifetime.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: These residents bought the property with the expectation that there will not be increased density in the area and that their views of the sea will not be obstructed.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, Singapore depends on skilled workers and professionals to build their HDB flats, condominiums, factories, office space, bus depots and Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) stations.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Without such skilled and competent workers, then the industry suffers as we will see the lowering of standards in the building and construction industry.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The feedback which I received from many members of the public is that there is lack of transparency in the works being carried out by contractors.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Yet, for a period of time, no work has been done and the place remains cordoned off.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: There is no update as to the timeline for completion of the works.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For my Mountbatten CC which is being rebuilt, the deadline for the issue of the Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) keeps being moved to a later date without any explanation as to the reason for the delay.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Surely, it makes more sense that once you start construction work on a site, the contractor should move quickly to carry out the work, complete the works expeditiously and then, the contractor can reinstate the site and move on to the next project.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, this does not seem to be the current situation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: After a site is cordoned off, many a times, no work is carried out for a period of time.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And the frequent reason given is that the contractor needs to get some permit or approval.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Will there be more support for construction firms so that we can have a pipeline of capable people in the industry?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: What about our efforts to attract engineers, architects and surveyors into the industry?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Chairman, Singapore has long engaged both international and local architects for major projects.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Some key examples: Jewel at Changi Airport, Marina Bay Sands and South Beach Development.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Countries, like China and Korea, initially collaborated with international firms but have since transitioned to having local architects spearhead significant developments.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Given Singapore's strong global reputation in urban planning, taking a similar approach could further strengthen the local architectural and design sectors.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Does the Government plan to entrust future major public projects solely to local firms, providing them greater opportunities to showcase their capabilities?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Additionally, are there initiatives to uplift Singapore's architectural and building design industry?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, the Minister recently announced the establishment of a task force to help sustain and grow heritage businesses.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: While some heritage businesses continue to flourish, many have decided to exit permanently owing to economic pressures, rising costs, lower consumer demand and also succession issues.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Ministry and URA elaborate on the plans to support heritage businesses in the short and longer term?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In particular, how can we help those where the next generation is committed to carry on but may need support in some areas?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Heritage businesses are a part of our shared history.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: As a community, we can all play our part by patronising heritage businesses.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: At its COS debate last year, the Minister spoke about the setting up of a tripartite workgroup for last-mile deliveries.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The workgroup had showcased developments at the URA Urban Lab Exhibition last November.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Ministry provide an update on the workgroup's progress and upcoming plans?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Louis Ng, please take your three cuts together.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Even as Minister Indranee swats and shoos me away, I keep coming back for more.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should clarify that the Minister actually does not always swat and shoo me away.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad our voices have been heard, and many current and future breastfeeding mothers will benefit from this change in policy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, for once, I shall not ask anymore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is 2025 and we should finally ensure that all our housing policies are inclusive and do not discriminate against single unwed parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why is their application on a case-by-case basis?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I can imagine how stressful it is to be a single unwed parent and our policies should help rather than discriminate against them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We ought to remember also that when we turn away a single unwed parent, are they really able to just rent in the open market, especially considering that many landlords do not want to rent to people with young children?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have spent a good part of my life calling for HDB to allow the keeping of cats in HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many have called for this and I am glad the Government has finally changed our policies and allow the keeping of cats in HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is still an outstanding issue of people breeding cats and abandoning them, and this puts our new policy in jeopardy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If this still cannot be done, then the Government should at least be given the power to mandate that someone has to sterilise their pet cats if the cats are found to cause disamenties in the community.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Joan Pereira, take your two cuts together, please.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: I shared about how residents of Skyville@Dawson had to put up with the disturbances and nuisance caused by inconsiderate visitors to the sky gardens at their HDB blocks.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The troubles my residents face continue to be year-round but are worse during the weekends, eve of festive seasons and public holidays.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Here are the top five complaints from my residents.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Groups of people regularly gather at the sky garden, making excessive noise late into the night, smoking and drinking.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: They show no regard for the people residing right next to the gardens.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Visitors have been urinating next to the staircase landing doors, with the pungent stench pervading all the surrounding homes.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: There is an increasing amount of litter and rubbish at the sky gardens and staircase landings.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Residents and I are aware that the gardens are public spaces.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: As I had highlighted before, public access is not a licence to abuse the usage of public spaces or behave inconsiderately and irresponsibly.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Over the last few years, we have worked with HDB, Town Council, Residents' Committees, the National Environment Agency (NEA) and the Police to solve these problems.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Hence, I appeal to MND to reconsider some of our previous suggestions.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: First, install gantries for registration, limit the number of visitors and require payment of fees to support the operations and cleaning of the sky gardens.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Registration will help to make visitors more conscious of how they behave.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: This method has been working well at another popular HDB rooftop terrace at the Pinnacle@Duxton.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Second, install more CCTVs to monitor visitors and their activities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Together with the registration, the video evidence will aid the relevant Government agencies for enforcement of illegal activities, whether it is for littering, vaping or public indecency.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The increasing number of hoarders in our residential estates are posing greater safety and health risks to our community.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The authorities are concerned that the problem of hoarding will worsen with our ageing population and had set up the New Environment Action Team (NEAT).

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: While I am heartened by this initiative, I urge MND to consider additional stricter measures concurrently.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Timely resolution of hoarding issues is important because: first, of the ever-present risks; and second, the lack of progress sends a signal that hoarders can do what they please without consequences.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: This leads to many helpless neighbours suffering for years.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Frustrated neighbours may lose faith in their community and the Government, and this is not at all helpful to building unity and neighbourly relations.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The broken windows theory states that visible signs of disorder will lead to more disorder as it gives the appearance that no one cares and no one is in charge, which can lead a neighbourhood to deteriorate very quickly.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: For those who suffer from mental health problems, sympathy for them does not mean that we disregard their or their neighbours' safety, health and well-being indefinitely.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Hence, hoarders with mental health issues should be required to accept professional assessment and treatment.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: For recalcitrant hoarders, MND may wish to consider introducing legislation to empower the authorities to relocate them.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Given that the pigeons are a potential health risk to residents, I urge NParks to do more to protect our residents from the possible health risks associated with pigeons.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: As Chairman of a Town Council, I keep receiving countless feedback about the mess left behind by pigeons.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: The pigeon faeces make a mess of the residents' clothes; make a mess on the windows, on the void deck; and pigeons would fly or walk into the food centre and attack the food while residents are having their meals.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Why are we so slow to do so even after the Town Council provides video evidence to NParks for enforcement?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: We can make the living environment better for all our residents if we take action against pigeon feeders promptly.

speaker: The Chairman:
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Chairman, perhaps only in Singapore are birds a major issue for the country's Members of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: But pest birds are a huge pain point for many of our residents, in many of our estates.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: And while the most effective way to manage the problem is to go upstream and control the pest bird population at source, by denying pest birds of their food sources in markets, hawker centres, coffeeshops and refuse collection centres; and by catching errant individuals who feed birds, including those who throw food out from out of their windows.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: We also need effective measures downstream, to quickly bring down a local pest bird population when it flares up from time to time, despite our upstream measures.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: So how does MND plan to strengthen our capabilities across the sector to manage this "birds problem" in our estates?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: How is the pilot going and is MSO planning to expand the pilot further?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Henry Kwek, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Chairman, recent high-profile animal cruelty cases highlighted a concerning trend in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: In fact, in one of the worst cases of animal cruelty recently, a Singaporean was found guilty of throwing community cats off HDB blocks, resulting in their deaths.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: This case underscores the pressing need for stronger animal welfare protection.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: These include 283 cases of cruelty with abandonment being the most common, followed by physical abuse.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And notably, there is a troubling increase in cases involving youths, rising from six in 2023 to 15 in 2024.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Can NParks provide more details on the specific areas under review and the implementation timeline?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Singapore's transformation into a City in Nature has been widely embraced by both Singaporeans and the global community.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Beyond enhancing greenery and biodiversity, this vision has strengthened our urban environment, public well-being and climate resilience.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: To sustain and deepen this impact, greater community involvement will be key.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: One way is to leverage on larger neighbourhood parks, such as the Hillock Linear Park within Kebun Bahru, to anchor Active Ageing Centers or introduce signature activities like monthly Sunday Markets for private estates, fostering social interaction and community engagement.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Another approach is for NParks to collaborate with the community to fund heritage displays in relevant parks.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: For example, working with the Hainan Clan Association to create mock-ups of the old village in the Thomson Nature Park.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: So, can NParks share its plans to involve more Singaporeans in the effort, empowering individuals, businesses and grassroots to get involved in NPark's City in Nature initiative?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Two, can there be sheltered playgrounds, exercise and fitness gyms with equipment suitable for young people and seniors to use, so that residents can keep fit with these facilities, whether it rains or shines?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Three, can there be a pets' corner, like a dog run, for pet-loving residents to bring their pets to enjoy the park too?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Four, can there be a walk-and-jog track separate from a cycling track, for the safety of both pedestrians and cyclists?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Five, can provision of space be made for a potential future MRT station at the corner this area, as it is strategically located opposite Fernvale, Cheng San-Seletar Hill and Jalan Kayu estates and which my fellow Ang Mo Kio GRC Members, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Ms Nadia Samdin and I have previously collectively hoped for and appealed to MOT for a feasibility study, to consider whether it can be done, so as to benefit Ang Mo Kio GRC residents living in all three constituencies in the future?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And lastly, when can all these discussions of the ideas above be started, with me as an advisor and Member of Parliament of Jalan Kayu and where the Sengkang West Industrial Estate is sited.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Nadia Samdin, please take your three cuts together.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Singapore is known around the world for integrating nature into our urban cityscape.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We take pride in our green efforts to keep us cool and our natural spaces are an essential part of our cultural identity as an island city-state.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am grateful to NParks and the wider MND family for these efforts.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can we have an update on the progress made on this front?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How will NParks continue to ramp up efforts, including maintaining and upgrading parks in private and public housing estates in a timely manner, to ensure equitable access to nature?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the past year, what has NParks done to involve more members of the community in our efforts to transform Singapore into a city in nature?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What are the key initiatives planned for 2025?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What is NParks doing to make green and blue spaces more accessible and inclusive for all Singaporeans?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Being a city in nature also means learning to co-exist with Singapore's diverse wildlife and understanding that we share this island that we all call home.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Yet, in the past years, we have had several encounters, from tapirs to crocodiles, otters to crows, chickens to koels.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our vision for every household to be within 10 minutes from a park, also means that inhabitants of the park are also 10 minutes from our households.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to ask how MND organises itself and community groups, to tackle these very real human-wildlife concerns, including disamenities caused by urban birds, while staying true to our desire to be a city in nature.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, in Ang Mo Kio, we have faced hygiene and noise challenges by pigeons, crows, chickens, mynahs and loss of fish from ponds, such as koi by otters, just to name a few.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What are some best-in-class practices which MND has adopted in maintaining the balance between intensifying and preserving greenery as well as ecosystems, while developing housing estates around green, blue and brown spaces.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I applaud NParks for this programme, especially given that corals form the backbone of many of our marine ecosystems.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can MND provide more details on the 100k Corals Initiative, were there any target species we are trying to revive during this programme?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And how will these efforts contribute to the diversity and vibrancy of our marine environment?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How can we better involve the public and interested volunteers, for example, through citizen science activities?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Has MND also considered whether mangrove trees, for example, can be part of our planted tree or coral programmes?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A key component of protecting our Blue Spaces is educating the public about the rich biodiversity surrounding our shores and empowering them to take a personal interest in conserving our waters.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To this end, groups, such as Friends of the Marine Park, play a critical role.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What are the updates that MND can share?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And how can we continue to interest Singaporeans to care for our Blue Spaces, as part of our island city-state identity?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our population is ageing and more people are choosing to remain single.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As this happens, the infrastructure in our housing estates must change to serve seniors' needs.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To this end, HDB has taken several decisive steps to support seniors with both their external and internal living environments.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I welcome the announcement, like many of my colleagues, to expand elements of EASE 2.0 to seniors not living in HDB flats.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How will MND assess households who may require the support?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In terms of their external living environment, what meaningful upgrades have been identified from community walks to be part of the Silver Upgrading Programme to transform our neighbourhood common spaces and encourage healthy living spans?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How can MND work with other agencies, for example, Town Council, LTA and NParks, to ensure that the features are done in a way that is not duplicative.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How is the Government continuing to improve the public rental scheme to support the evolving needs of Singaporeans, including reviewing the qualifying criteria?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Some rental families in Woodlands have highlighted to me the challenges they face with the scheme.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Some are not eligible, for example, single parents and first-timers, who form a not insignificant and growing share of new public rental households today.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Others are eligible but continue to struggle with financial stability or continuous employment and find the upfront of regular payments difficult.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: They are looking for higher grants or extended loan tenures.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: ComLink+-style support in terms of financial counselling and employment support would also help.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: To that end, can the Minister provide an update on the take-up and success rate of the scheme to-date?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: How else can the Government support more low-income families that are currently renting to buy their home?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Further, would the Government consider extending the Fresh Start Housing Scheme to families that are really struggling but not staying in public rental, as is being considered for the ComLink+ plans?

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Chairman, at the start of this term of Government, we faced significant challenges brought on by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It was against this backdrop that I outlined the Ministry of National Development's (MND's) priorities during the Debate on the President's Address in 2020.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, we committed to keep public housing affordable, accessible and inclusive.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we said that we will transform Singapore into a City in Nature, one that is more liveable and sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, we would continue uplifting our Built Environment (BE) sector, to make it more productive and resilient.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We worked with colleagues, stakeholders and the community to deliver on these priorities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, I will speak on housing as well as the BE sector transformation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague, Second Minister Indranee Rajah, will cover long-term planning for our city and support for our construction firms.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will share our efforts to enhance our living environment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How will touch on how we are transforming Singapore into a City in Nature, and Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim will speak about what we are doing for lower-income households.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the past few years, we grappled with significant housing challenges.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Fear of housing delays also caused demand to spike.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, there was a broad-based increase in demand driven by changing social norms.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Application rates for Build-To-Order (BTO) flats spiked and Housing and Development Board (HDB) resale prices rose sharply.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We rolled out various measures over the last few years to address this supply-demand imbalance.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, we pushed hard to complete the flats delayed by COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is the equivalent of two Ang Mo Kio towns in less than five years, despite the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have shortened the median waiting times for BTO flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In 2024, the median waiting time was less than four years, comparable to the pre-COVID-19 norm of three to four years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We had also previously committed that by 2025, we will build 2,000 to 3,000 shorter waiting time flats, which are flats with a waiting time of two-plus years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We met this target one year ahead of schedule when we launched more than 2,800 shorter waiting time flats last year in 2024.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This means that first-timer families applying for BTO flats are more likely to receive an invitation to book a flat today than it was before the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: On the private housing front, we have increased supply through the Government Land Sales (GLS) programme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In 2024, we released land for around 11,000 private housing units, which is the highest in a single year since 2013.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a result, the private housing market started to ease in recent years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This year, we will launch more than 25,000 flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This includes 19,600 BTO flats and more than 5,500 Sale of Balance flats (SBF) flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will also raise private housing supply from the GLS programme to around 8,500 units in the first half of 2025, with more to come later this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: From 2025 to 2027, we will launch more than 50,000 BTO flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will also continue to shorten waiting times.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This year, we will launch another 3,800 Shorter Waiting Time flats (SWT).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This means that 20% of all BTO flats launched this year in 2025 will be a SWT flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We launched our largest ever SBF exercise last month, and we will be launching another SBF exercise later this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These flats will cover a wide range of locations.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This year alone, HDB will be launching BTO flats in around 60% of our towns and estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Singaporeans can also look forward to more flats in attractive locations, such as Mount Pleasant.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It will be near the future Mount Pleasant Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station on the Thomson East Coast Line.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There will be an eating house and a supermarket within the precinct.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Residents will be able to cycle to MacRitchie Reservoir to enjoy nature.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Toa Payoh Town Centre and the future Toa Payoh Integrated Development will not be far away, with supermarkets, a polyclinic, a library, sports facilities and more.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The new estate will be inspired by the area's rich heritage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Six buildings from the Old Police Academy have been conserved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Even as we ramp up supply, we have kept new flats affordable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have increased market subsidies for BTO flats to keep them affordable for households, with a wide range of incomes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also raised the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG) last year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As a result in 2024, more than eight in 10 first-timer families who collected keys to their BTO flats were able to service their HDB loans using their their Central Provident Fund (CPF), with little to no cash outlay.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have taken major steps to ensure that public housing in attractive locations like Mount Pleasant remain affordable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This also ensures that they remain inclusive, an important part of Singapore's social compact, so that Singaporeans of different backgrounds and income levels can live in the same neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, we need to reduce the lottery effect for those who successfully ballot for such flats, to keep the system of subsidies fair.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is something Miss Cheryl Chan had asked about.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We took the first major step four years ago with the Prime Location Public Housing (PLH) model in 2021.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This allows us to unlock new, choicier areas for affordable public housing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Take the Redhill area near the MRT station, for example.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is currently built up with private residential properties etched in pink.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These can be expensive as Redhill is a highly sought-after location.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But HDB launched Alexandra Vale in 2022, and then Alexandra Peaks in 2023 in the same area, all under the PLH model.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
