text: In July 2025, we will be launching another two BTO projects in the area under the new flat classification framework, one next to Alexandra Peaks and another along Tanglin Road.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One of the blocks in Alexandra Peaks will also house public rental flats, allowing lower-income households access to public rental options in these prime areas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In October last year, Mr Chua Heng Wee and Ms Shermaine Ho, a young couple, applied for a 4-room BTO Plus flat in Merpati Alcove, in Macpherson.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They were successful and booked a flat on a high floor early this year, for around $620,000, before grants.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Merpati Alcove is in a very good location, right at the doorstep of Mattar MRT station and within walking distance to the Circuit Road Food Centre.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With a combined income of around $7,800 today, they received an EHG of $20,000 and were able to service their mortgage with low cash outlay.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For prime flats, let us look at Tanjong Rhu Parc Front in Tanjong Rhu, which we launched last month.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is a very attractive project near the city centre and a short distance from the riverfront.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A 4-room BTO Prime flat in that project is around $640,000, before grants.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A couple with a combined income of $8,500 would receive an EHG of $10,000 and will be able to service their mortgage with a monthly cash outlay of about $180.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is what we mean when we say that we will seek to ensure a wide range of affordable housing options for Singaporeans with different housing budgets.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Singaporeans have been anxious about resale flat prices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked how resale flats can be kept affordable for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I mentioned earlier that the supply-demand imbalance had led to high resale prices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In these past few years, we have also seen fewer flats reaching their minimum occupation period (MOP), due to fewer flat completions during the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, in 2020, HDB should have completed 20,000 flats, but because of the disruptions by the pandemic, we completed fewer than half of that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, five years on in 2025, with much fewer flats completing their MOP and even fewer flats going on the resale market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The supply tightness should start to recover next year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The cooling measures that we implemented will also continue to work their way through the market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Taken together, the HDB resale market will stabilise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also improve housing accessibility for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But let me assure first-timer families that we will continue to prioritise you for new flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, we tighten the rules on non-selection of flats, to give priority for those with genuine, pressing housing needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Next, we also introduced the First-timer (Parents and Married Couples) (or FT(PMC)) category.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Take Ms Nicole Chong and Mr Christopher Edward Sean.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They decided to solemnise their marriage before applying for their flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This made them eligible for the FT(PMC) category.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With that, they managed to book their 4-room Standard flat in Sengkang on their very first try!

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nicole and Christopher are just one of the many couples who have benefited from these priority schemes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This means that virtually all of them were given the chance to book a flat within two tries in categories where they are given first priority.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have also provided more support to families who need a place to stay while waiting to collect their keys.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, we provide subsidised temporary housing through the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we have come a long way since 2021, when we started out with 800 PPHS flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether the Government will consider allowing single unwed parents to qualify for PPHS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To all single parents who have needs, HDB will not turn away your request for housing assistance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will take a holistic approach to every case and, depending on the needs, we may assist with interim rental housing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, for those who are eligible for the schemes that I have mentioned, they likely can book a flat on their first or second try, based on current trends.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Then, they can apply for temporary subsidised rental housing through the PPHS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If they booked a SWT flat, they will be able to collect their keys in two-plus years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked how we plan to keep housing affordable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Aside from first-timer families, we recognise that there are more singles looking to own their own home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over the years, we have provided singles with greater access to public housing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the past, singles 35 and above were only allowed to buy HDB resale flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Then in 2013, the Government allowed first-timer singles to purchase new 2-room BTO flats, but only in non-mature estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In recent years, we have made further moves.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: From October last year, we allowed first-timer singles to apply for 2-room Flexi BTO flats island-wide, including in Prime and Plus locations, and not just Standard.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Just last month, one in four of the flats offered at the launch was a 2-room Flexi flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: From the middle of this year, we will move beyond just access, to providing priority access for singles who wish to live near or with their parents, under the new Family Care Scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also want to look at the needs of other groups, including second-timer families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In 2022, we had reduced the proportion of BTO supply set aside for second-timer families in order to better prioritise first-timer families because, if Members remember then, first-timer application rates had increased significantly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Application rates for first-timer families have come down.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also hear the concerns of second-timer families who need to buy another subsidised flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This change will take effect from the July 2025 BTO exercise, that is, the next BTO exercise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB will release more details closer to the date.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We do not expect significant impact on the application rates for first-timer families as we are continuing to build more BTO flats to meet demand.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to review our policies to see if there is scope to improve access further for different groups, such as singles and others.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Miss Cheryl Chan have also asked if we can raise our BTO and Executive Condominium (EC) income ceilings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our BTO income ceiling today still covers about eight in 10 Singaporean households.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: New flats and housing subsidies are prioritised for those who need them more.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Those within and above this income bracket, can also choose from a wide range of resale HDB flats or private residential properties, for which there is no income ceiling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to keep an eye on income growth and market conditions, and will raise the income ceilings when the time is right.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our second priority is to keep public housing inclusive.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to support the housing needs of different segments of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One segment is our lower-income and vulnerable households, who do not have other housing options and family support at this time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are making significant moves through the Fresh Start Housing Scheme to support public rental tenants on their home ownership journey, as Prime Minister Lawrence Wong had announced during his Budget Statement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My colleague, Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim, will share more details later.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under the Age Well SG programme, we are making our environment more senior-friendly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Carrie Tan and Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin had asked about this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the HDB estate level, we will be introducing senior-friendly enhancements for selected HDB estates under the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) and the Silver Upgrading Programme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These include fitness trails to support healthy living, as well as rest points along pathways to boost walkability.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Within the home, HDB offers subsidised senior-friendly fittings under the Enhancement for Active Seniors programme (EASE).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These fittings help to improve the mobility and safety of seniors in their own homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We expanded the range of subsidised fittings under EASE 2.0 last year, to include fittings like foldable U-grab bars, home fire alarm devices and more.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Since EASE and EASE 2.0 were introduced, about 340,000 households have signed up.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Beyond HDB estates, we also plan to help seniors in private residential properties age-in-place.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Henry Kwek, Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Denise Phua asked for more details.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have expanded the scope of the Estate Upgrading Programme (EUP) to include senior-friendly enhancements, such as barrier-free ramps and covered drains for more walkways.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also have a new EUP for Silver Estates, so that these benefits can reach selected estates that have benefited from EUP some time ago.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will do more to improve the safety and mobility of our seniors living in private homes within their own home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will introduce a new programme, EASE(Private), as the Prime Minister had announced during Budget.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I remember Ms Denise Phua and Ms Ng Ling Ling asking MND last year to consider this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Aside from improvements to the estate and home, we understand that Singaporeans are also concerned about retirement adequacy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We hear the concerns that those who buy older resale flats might not have saved enough for retirement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But do not worry, we have a system in place today to help home buyers balance between meeting their housing and retirement needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And a home is also a store of value for retirement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For those who buy older resale flats, there are limits placed on the use of the CPF Ordinary Account, as well as the amount of HDB housing loan taken.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The money set aside can then be used to help home buyers meet their retirement needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The generous housing grants received by eligible first-timer home buyers are also refunded into their own CPF account when they sell their flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, seniors can unlock the value of their flats to supplement their retirement income through a number of ways.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, seniors can consider renting out their flat or spare bedroom.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They can opt to sell part of their lease back to HDB through the Lease Buyback Scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Seniors can also choose to right-size to a smaller home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will do more for seniors who wish to right-size for their retirement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, the Government provides a Silver Housing Bonus (SHB), of up to $30,000 in cash when seniors right-size to a 3-room or smaller flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will make three changes to the SHB, which will take effect from 1 December 2025.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This will bring the maximum bonus quantum from $30,000 currently to $40,000.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, we will extend the scheme to more seniors living in private residential properties, with annual values between $21,000 and $31,000.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They will receive a bonus of up to $10,000 if they right-size to a 3-room HDB flat and up to $20,000 if they purchase a 2-room HDB flat or Community Care Apartment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With this enhancement, more than 15,000 more seniors can qualify for the SHB.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Altogether, the Silver Housing Bonus scheme will cover more than three in four residential properties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, we will adjust the cash top-up requirement so that seniors will qualify for the SHB as long as they commit to a net increase of up to $60,000 in their CPF Retirement Account after right-sizing, for their retirement payouts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This amount can come from their CPF housing refunds, which means that seniors may no longer need to make a cash top-up to qualify for the SHB.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This will make it easier for seniors to benefit from the Silver Housing Bonus.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chairman, our third priority is to rejuvenate our towns.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some Members have asked about the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme (VERS).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: VERS will be one of the ways to enable our towns to be revitalised to refresh the age profile of our public housing stock.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When the concept of VERS was first announced back in 2018, we made it clear that VERS will not start until the 2030s, when our first flats are around the 70-year mark.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are no such flats today, nor any within this decade.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: VERS is a complex and long-term undertaking and is one of a number of programmes that we will need to rejuvenate and reimagine our public housing estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We need to carefully and sensitively stage the programme to reduce disamenities to residents living in newer parts of towns.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, we need to ensure that there are enough homes for those who need to relocate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will share more details on the mechanics, processes and packages for VERS in due course and seek views from Singaporeans in the process.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The HIP is today our flagship programme for tackling common maintenance issues faced in our older estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under the HIP essential improvements, like repairs to spalling concrete, are fully funded by the Government.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Looking ahead, we are working with industry partners and research institutes to develop better ways to address maintenance issues in our old estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As our homes get older, issues, such as spalling concrete and external wall seepage, can be destructive to residents' daily lives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, we want to make repairs more durable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, HDB introduced the corrosion resistant repair (CRR) method last year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: CRR helps to reduce the recurrence of spalling concrete.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, we want to improve diagnosis methods, so that we can more accurately pinpoint the root cause of the issue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In complex cases, it can be difficult to identify exactly the source of seepage and the extent of repairs needed through visual checks alone.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB has started trialling the use of better scanning technology.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Similar to an x-ray machine, it allows us to see beneath the surface, to try to trace the root cause of the seepage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If successful, residents can look forward to faster and more accurate diagnosis and swifter repair works.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will trial this technology starting with some 70 flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Then, we will see if this technology can be scaled up for widespread use.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, we will develop early detection technology, such as predictive data analytics.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This allows HDB to put in preventative measures and develop more targeted programmes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB will progressively launch grant calls to develop ideas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also ensure that the technology we develop will be put to good use, by helping out Town Councils and private contractors to strengthen their capabilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about our plans to accelerate sector transformation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Currently, to ensure timely injection of housing supply, most housing developers are required to commence construction within two years, and complete construction and sell all units within five years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Failing which, the upfront remittable ABSD component will be clawed back.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will therefore extend the ABSD remission timeline for housing developers undertaking these projects.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This includes projects that: transform our urban environment at a large scale; optimise land through intensification or integration with other developments including major public infrastructure; rejuvenate older estates; or adopt new technologies to achieve higher productivity targets.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Through this, we want to encourage housing developers and their alliances or firms to undertake projects that will transform our built environment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Details will be released in a statement later today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This will be used to enhance enterprise capabilities, adoption of advanced technologies and the building of firms’ manpower capabilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My colleague, Minister Indranee Rajah, will share more about our efforts to transform the built environment sector in her speech.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chairman, if you allow, in Mandarin, please.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: (In Mandarin):   This year marks Singapore's 60th year of Independence.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For 60 years, the Government has stayed true to its mission of providing homes for our people.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This commitment has never changed and will not waver.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, some elderly parents worry whether their children will be able to afford and purchase homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want to assure these parents that we have implemented various measures to ensure their children can afford and acquire homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In January this year, we successfully completed all pandemic-delayed HDB projects, delivering over 75,000 HDB units.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have also reduced waiting times for new HDB projects.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Last year, the waiting time for new flats was less than four years, similar to pre-pandemic levels.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Overall, the application rates for first-timer families for BTO flats are lower than pre-pandemic levels.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Last year, we increased the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant to ensure low- and middle-income first-time homebuyers can afford HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These families can receive up to $120,000 in grants when purchasing BTO flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Last year's data also shows that most first-time homebuyers can use their CPF to pay their monthly instalments, with only minimal cash outlay required and some not needing to use any cash at all.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Although the situation has stabilised, the Government will continue to launch many HDB flats for Singaporeans to apply for.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These shorter waiting time flats make up one-fifth of total supply.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also launch another round of Sale of Balance Flats later this year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Many are familiar with the Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programme and have received Government subsidies to install elderly-friendly features, like grab bars and ramps, in their homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will extend the EASE programme to elderly households living in private properties to make their home environment more accessible and safer.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The programme will begin early next year for a period of three years, with details to be announced later.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to address common maintenance issues in older HDB flats through the Home Improvement Programme, such as spalling concrete and external wall seepage, while continuing to develop more inspection technologies and repair methods.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For retired seniors who wish to monetise their flats to supplement their living expenses, we will provide more assistance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will enhance the Silver Housing Bonus scheme to benefit more seniors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This means the maximum bonus they can receive will increase from the current $30,000 to $40,000.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Currently, elderly homeowners need to use cash proceeds from their flat sale to top up their CPF Retirement Account to receive the bonus.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Homeowners can use the CPF refund from their flat sale to top-up their CPF Retirement Account.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This way, seniors may no longer need to use cash to be eligible for the Silver Housing Bonus.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our pioneers' foresight laid a strong foundation that allows us to enjoy high-quality living today; our homeownership rate is among the highest globally.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is our promise to Singaporeans: whether it is you, your children or grandchildren, everyone will be able to have a safe haven, living and pursuing their dreams in a warm and harmonious environment. : Mr Chairman, let me conclude.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At MND, we have had the privilege to work with many talented architects, planners, builders, dedicated colleagues, industry partners, conservationists, NGOs, nature groups, and so on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They have contributed to making Singapore a distinctive global city and an enduring home for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Five years ago, we plunged into crisis mode.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: COVID-19 had long-tail effects, particularly for construction, but we have caught up and we have sought to address as many pain points as possible.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are on track to launch more than 130,000 flats over seven years from 2021 to 2027.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have shortened BTO waiting times this year to the pre-COVID-19 norm.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: BTO application rates are now lower than during pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We opened up access to singles and will be restoring some of the access for second-timer families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the HDB resale market, we implemented cooling measures and ramped up the supply of flats, which will stabilise the market over time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, we have worked to prepare for the longer term.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We introduced the New Flat Classification Framework during the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In doing so, we ensure social mixing in different parts of Singapore now and in the future.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are also planning bigger moves for areas such as Mount Pleasant, Greater Southern Waterfront, Paya Lebar Airbase and Turf City.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This will create more space for Singaporeans, for their homes, dreams and aspirations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As Singapore grows and develops, we have also been deliberate in ensuring that we conserve nature and protect our heritage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Given our very limited land and resources, this is not an easy feat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It requires thoughtful and disciplined long-term planning, building on the good work of our predecessors to dream bigger for the future, and to dream sustainably.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is an ongoing journey and Singapore will always be a work in progress.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And through it all, we will continue working with Singaporeans as custodians and stakeholders to shape our social compact and achieve our shared vision to create a home where Singaporeans can thrive, where no one is left behind.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is our enduring commitment for an endearing home.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, we have transformed our city and our island in the last 60 years, despite our limited land.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is enabled by our integrated planning framework, which allows agencies to coordinate land use and development needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Agencies also closely engage citizens and industry, enabling active participation from stakeholders.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will need to push the boundaries for productivity, sustainability and resiliency, to keep Singapore a liveable city for many generations to come.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Master Plan is a statutory plan that translates longer-term land use strategies from the Long-Term Plan into detailed plans and policies to guide physical development over the next 10 to 15 years.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is instrumental to shaping our city’s future, by balancing economic, social and environmental considerations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These engagements have generated greater awareness and appreciation amongst Singaporeans of the complexities and challenges of land use planning in Singapore, which require balancing housing, jobs, green spaces, infrastructure and heritage, all within our limited land and sea space.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Given the DMP’s importance, we encourage all Singaporeans to participate in the ongoing engagements.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Given its scale and complexity, we need to start our preparations for "Long Island" as soon as possible.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have initiated technical studies, including environmental studies, while simultaneously engaging stakeholders and members of the public to gather ideas and suggestions.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Beyond infrastructure, we want to create spaces where we can feel connected to one another and the environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This involves preserving our built heritage so that we have a physical anchor to our past and memories.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Keith Chua has asked how the Government will support heritage businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Led by Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim and Senior Minister of State for the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth and the Ministry of Trade and Industry Low Yen Ling, the task force aims to strengthen support for heritage businesses and traditional activities so that our built heritage areas retain their character and “soul”.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth or Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling will share more about this task force at MCCY’s Committee of Supply (COS) debate.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked how public feedback, especially on high-rise developments in built-up residential areas, is incorporated into our plans, such as those at Amber Road.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In land-scarce Singapore, we have to optimise our limited land resources to meet a wide range of diverse needs, including housing, transportation and community spaces.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is especially important for work and residential areas nearer to MRT stations, including the Amber Road area near the newly completed Tanjong Katong TEL station, which can allow more residents to enjoy the convenience of living near transport nodes and amenities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government will study the feedback raised, such as on density and traffic, and consider mitigating measures where feasible.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With careful planning and thoughtful design, we will continue to safeguard a quality living environment for all Singaporeans, while balancing our diverse land use needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Louis Chua asked how the Government can enhance amenities and infrastructure to enhance liveability and inclusiveness in Sengkang.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These will be factored into and featured at the upcoming DMP2025 exhibition, which is the culmination of our public engagements, from June 2025 onwards.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The DMP2025 exhibition will display our planning vision, strategies and development plans for the next 10 to 15 years and be brought to various locations island-wide.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We encourage everyone to visit the DMP2025 exhibition.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next, I move to our plans to build a strong and dynamic built environment (BE) sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The last five years were not easy for the BE sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The sector was severely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This experience has strengthened our resolve to transform the BE sector, which has been so pivotal to Singapore’s development.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With advancements in science and technology, the BE sector is moving from bricks and mortar to smart technology, encompassing AI-assisted tools, automation and digital collaboration across the construction lifecycle, from planning and design, to construction and inspection.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: CORENET X, a one-stop digital platform that streamlines regulatory approvals, allows architects and engineers to ensure regulatory compliance more easily and focus on innovation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the construction phase, firms are also deploying technological solutions to improve worker safety.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, Zheng Keng Engineering and Construction has incorporated AI into their onsite safety surveillance system, so site managers can intervene immediately during risky situations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: BCA has also recently implemented virtual Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) inspections through virtual scans, as an alternative inspection option to conventional, physical site inspections.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are working with agencies to expand these efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: BE firms can receive up to 70% funding support to develop enterprise capabilities, technology adoption and manpower capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I strongly encourage firms to approach BCA for more information and to apply.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government will also continue to encourage our local construction industry to adopt productive technologies.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are reviewing the types of construction facilities supported by the LIA and will share more details when ready.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the heart of any successful sector are the people, in this case, the built environment professionals – the architects, engineers, quantity surveyors and more.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is why we have set up the Taskforce for Architectural and Engineering Consultants in September 2024, co-led by myself and Mr Chaly Mah, Chairman of Surbana Jurong Group.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Over the last few months, the task force has been engaging a wide range for stakeholders, including young professionals and firms in the BE sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We were heartened to learn that young BE professionals gain immense satisfaction from contributing to Singapore’s built environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They take pride in designing and constructing buildings that improve the lives of future generations – a hospital that cares for the sick, a school that nurtures the next generation, or a landmark that puts Singapore on the world map.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, professionals have also expressed concerns on the sector’s pay, career development opportunities and HR support.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have also heard that some firms put in lowly-priced tender bids at the expense of quality and business sustainability.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, the task force is looking at how we can strengthen and support the BE consultancy trade associations and chambers (TACs), such as the Singapore Institute of Architects (SIA) and the Association of Consulting Engineers Singapore (ACES), to play a greater role in uplifting the sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The TACs are critical if we are to succeed.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The task force will study how to help our TACs build up their capabilities, including areas, such as sector branding, catalysing members’ adoption of technology and capability building.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, the task force aims to make the BE sector a career of choice for talented Singaporeans passionate about shaping Singapore’s physical development.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have also heard our youths’ concerns on the sector’s pay and appeal.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In response, the task force is working with the firms, TACs, Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) and professional boards to enhance internship experiences and review the starting salaries for fresh graduates.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Several progressive firms, such as Arup Singapore, Beca, DP Architects and ID Architects, have already put these in place and we encourage more firms to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To Miss Rachel Ong’s question, our agencies actively facilitate opportunities for our local architects to participate in public sector projects and showcase their capabilities, through design competitions and tenders.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many local architectural firms have put forth innovative design proposals for unique projects of varying scales and types, ranging from landmark developments, such as the Pinnacle@Duxton, new civic and public spaces, like Geylang Serai Cultural Belt, to signature buildings, such as the upcoming NS Square.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, the task force has heard that some firms tended to put in lowly-priced tender bids at the expense of quality and business sustainability.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To address this, the Government has been progressively enhancing our tender evaluation approaches to deter fee-diving and strengthen the quality-based procurement criteria.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also review our procurement contracts to ensure a fairer balance of risks between service buyers and BE consultants.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Beyond public sector projects, we strongly encourage the private sector service buyers to enhance your procurement practices.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will give the industry greater assurance to compete on quality, offer differentiated value propositions, and invest in human capital, technologies and innovation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Fourth, we want our BE consultants to harness the ongoing technological revolution to grow their capabilities, profits and careers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, SAA Architects, a Singapore home-grown firm, has been able to speed up its early design processes by leveraging GenAI-powered automation tools.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This lets them focus on higher value work, such as analysis and study of their designs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Harnessing technologies can also improve BE consultants’ career prospects.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: When Mr Muhammad Khalil started his career as a draftsman in 2025, manual drawing was still prevalent.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Over the years, Mr Khalil upskilled to use technologies, such as building information models (BIM) and AI tools, which opened up new career opportunities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, Mr Khalil is a Senior Vice President at Boustead Projects, where he partners developers, builders and fellow consultants to leverage digital technologies to deliver building projects more efficiently.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I encourage firms to tap on these resources to accelerate their transformation journeys.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The task force will continue working on these highlighted areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our efforts will also address some of the feedback that businesses have provided to the Inter-Ministerial Committee for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We welcome further inputs ahead of our finalised recommendations in the second half of 2025.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As we revitalise and build our city, we must ensure its inclusiveness to different segments of our society.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As such, we had convened a Code Review Committee, to review the Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Code review seeks to address the current gaps and anticipate the future needs of persons with disabilities (PwDs), the elderly and young families with children.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, enhancements to lactation room standards to better support the needs of breastfeeding mothers have been proposed.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In addition, we will continue to provide funding support through the Accessibility Fund, to encourage owners of existing older buildings to upgrade their premises with inclusive features.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We thank the public for your views during our consultation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Code will be finalised and released in the second quarter of 2025 and the industry will be given sufficient lead time before the Code takes effect.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Ong Hua Han asked whether the Government would consider extending the benefits of HDB’s Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programme to PwDs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While EASE is designed to meet the needs of seniors, we understand that EASE may also be helpful for other HDB residents with mobility challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: HDB assesses applications from those who do not meet the eligibility criteria on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Social agencies and healthcare professionals may advise PwDs staying in HDB flats to approach HDB for assistance if they are looking for in-home fittings.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and SG Enable also have a suite of existing initiatives to support PwDs to live independently in the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, in conclusion, our future is shaped by the collective efforts of every segment of society.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I urge each of you to actively participate in the upcoming Draft Master Plan Exhibition and our other initiatives that will contribute to shaping Singapore’s urban landscape, as part of our continuous efforts to revitalise and enhance our home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their cuts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I will speak on four areas: first, maintaining affordable cooked food options in the neighbourhood; second, making physical enhancements to our neighbourhoods to take care of the needs of more users; third, improving the delivery of municipal services; and lastly, resolving complex community challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Mr Henry Kwek will be pleased to hear that our Budget Meal initiative has made good progress since it was announced in March 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This means budget meals can now be found at many more heartland locations throughout the island.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If we were to draw a radius of 400 metres or about five to 10 minutes walking distance around every coffeeshop offering budget meals, more than 80% of HDB flats would be covered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Credit goes to the collective efforts of the Community Development Councils, HDB and Enterprise Singapore for achieving this coverage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In particular, the agencies jointly encouraged nine coffeeshop chain operators to come onboard the Community Budget Meal initiative in July 2024.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: All these stalls offering budget meals can be found on the BudgetMealGoWhere portal, a collaboration between HDB and GovTech, that allows users to search for the nearest coffeeshop with budget meal options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since its launch, the BudgetMealGoWhere portal has been well-received, and has recorded more than 450,000 unique visitors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To reach out to more people, including seniors who may not be active online, MND and HDB have publicised the budget meal initiative via mainstream media, including newspapers and radio channels, and will continue to explore ways to raise awareness on the availability of budget meals in HDB estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since December 2023, new buyers of privately-owned HDB coffee shops will need to offer budget meals once they have taken over the coffee shop.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Eight coffee shops now provide budget meals in line with this requirement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This will enable more residents to have access to affordable cooked food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While ensuring affordable cooked food options for Singaporeans, we do not wish to overburden our local food businesses, particularly stallholders running small or micro-businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To this end, we are studying two key moves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Details of these changes will be announced at a later date.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Next, let me share on how we are enhancing the inclusiveness of our neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Jean See, Ms Joan Pereira, Ms Denise Phua and the Leader of the Opposition, all spoke on this from the perspective of different stakeholder groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked about spaces that allowed for intergenerational exchange, and for people with special needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We actively partner the community in the design and upgrading of our neighbourhood spaces to ensure that they are inclusive to people of all age groups and capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, under the Silver Upgrading Progamme (SUP), agencies will engage residents through a community walk, to identify gaps and seek their suggestions for improvement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This may include adding senior-friendly mobility enhancements like rest points and barrier-free access ramps along frequented routes, dementia-friendly features to improve wayfinding, as well as wheelchair-friendly therapeutic gardens and three-generational amenities to promote inter-generational interaction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, we also work closely with community partners to ensure that seniors and the vulnerable are well supported if their flat has been chosen for the Selective En bloc Redevelopment Scheme (SERS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, for SERS in Ang Mo Kio, every household is assigned a journey manager who proactively reaches out to provide relocation assistance especially to seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Seniors are guided throughout the entire SERS process from announcement to key collection and flat return.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Where needed, journey managers work with other agencies such as People's Association (PA), Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and MSF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Households who would like to continue living close to their neighbours in the designated replacement site can do so by applying for their replacement flats under the Joint Selection Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the past year, our Tripartite Workgroup has engaged over 2,000 stakeholders, from delivery personnel to developers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For greater awareness, URA will rove the exhibition on innovative last-mile delivery practices to heartland malls in the next few months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As the Workgroup continues to study more ways to improve last-mile deliveries, we encourage more stakeholders and residents to co-create solutions suited for different locations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Joan Pereira raised on behalf of her residents the issue of disamenities in residential sky gardens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB will continue to work with the Member, Town Councils and NEA on various efforts to minimise disamenities to residents, while keeping communal spaces open and accessible for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We urge everyone to be considerate in their use of communal spaces, including sky gardens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Denise Phua asked about support for condominium living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Resources on best practices in estate management and support for dispute resolution are available, such as Strata Management Guides issued by BCA, industry-led accreditation schemes for Managing Agents as well as the Strata Titles Boards (STB) which mediate and hear disputes related to strata-titled properties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To the query by the Leader of the Opposition, the funds granted to each town by the Community Improvement Projects Committee (CIPC), depends on three factors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, the number of HDB flats in the town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Larger towns with more residents will be allocated more resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, the number and value of projects submitted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The CIPC will evaluate projects in the rank order submitted by the Town Councils (TCs) and Citizens’ Consultative Committees (CCCs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, whether the submitted projects meet eligibility criteria.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, projects that are not value for money, or cater only to specific interest groups or commercial entities will be rejected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Broadly speaking, larger towns that submit more projects amounting to higher values get more funding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Where they are rejected, there are two reasons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One, they did not meet the eligibility criteria; or two, they were lower-ranked projects from towns which submitted a total project value far exceeding what would have been commensurate with the number of flats in their town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For such projects, TCs and CCCs can resubmit them in subsequent years with higher rank orders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So far, we have completed three funding cycles for FY2021, FY2022 and FY2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For FY2024, we have completed the first stage of in-principle approval.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: From experience, the final funding for FY2024 may be slightly lower if TCs and CCCs eventually decide, for their own reasons, not to proceed with some of the supported projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These are larger towns ranging from 69,000 to 104,000 HDB flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Most of these are smaller towns, ranging from 39,000 to 53,000 HDB flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I looked into why Aljunied-Hougang has been receiving less CIPC funding than other towns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The reason is that it has consistently submitted fewer projects than the rest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example in FY2024, each town on average submitted 53 projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On average, the CIPC approved about 39 projects at about $4 million per town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Sengkang submitted the most projects, 248 projects worth $30 million or about half of the more than $60 million funding approved across all towns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Given funding constraints, the CIPC could only support 47 of Sengkang's higher-ranked projects amounting to $4.5 million.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The CIPC is happy to clarify with any TC or CCC if they have queries on their rejected proposals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In fact, the CIPC has regularly provided explanations to TCs and CCCs that requested such information and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In February 2022, we started the Integrated Municipal Operations Pilot in Tampines Town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The pilot centralised the delivery of 10 common municipal services under a single operator, where they used to be done by multiple contractors under different Ministries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This includes services, such as cleaning and infrastructure maintenance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Under the pilot, the active use of operations-technology (ops-tech) solutions, coupled with the cross-skilling of municipal workers, has enabled them to take on more related tasks with a leaner, more productive workforce, while also addressing issues more pre-emptively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have reaped good results at our first pilot site and have expanded the integrated ops to Pasir Ris-Punggol, to see if we could achieve similar efficiencies over a larger area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To address Mr Xie Yao Quan's question, the expanded pilot continued to yield good results.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Given the positive results, we are gathering learning points and studying how to refine and expand the model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have begun proactively engaging industry partners to share our findings and understand what other capabilities can be tapped on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The trickiest municipal issues tend to involve changing human behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Joan Pereira has asked for stricter measures to deal with hoarding cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These have already been included in amendments to the Community Disputes Resolution Act last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Where the hoarder has a suspected mental health condition, the pilot Community Relations Unit (CRU) will work with mental health professionals from relevant agencies and community partners to refer such cases for the appropriate mental health assessment and support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We know that the underlying motivations and support networks of hoarders and their families vary from case to case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is no one-size-fits-all solution and enforcement is only one of the several measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The New Environment Action Team (NEAT) will continue to develop and refine our strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While ensuring Singaporeans have access to budget meals, we do not want to overburden our local F&B operators, especially stallholders running small businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Further details will be announced when ready. : These initiatives reflect our commitment to partnering with stakeholders, like residents and business owners, in shaping enduring, vibrant communities and ensuring our neighbourhoods remain desirable places to call home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We invite Members of this House to join us in this endeavour and encourage active participation within your constituencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have come far since our Garden City days and are now transforming Singapore into a City in Nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin has asked for progress updates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are continuing to expand our green spaces and bring them closer to every resident.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: National Parks Board (NParks) will continue expanding its network of parks and park connectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also progressively carrying out concept studies on over 100 hectares of potential park development area in the coming years, with a view to bring more green spaces closer to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These complement our plans to enhance 13 Southwestern parks, including transforming three of the parks into Destination Parks and the rejuvenation and greening of Orchard Road.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Last year, we announced plans to designate a second marine park at Lazarus South and Kusu Reef.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To answer Ms Nadia's query, we are working with the nature community, experts and other agencies on detailed site studies, to inform the designation of the second marine park.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Nadia and Miss Cheryl Chan asked about accessibility and inclusivity of our green and common spaces, and how we can cater spaces for active living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have made a concerted effort to make our green spaces more accessible and inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Our network of green spaces with therapeutic gardens, landscapes and pro-health features enriches our interactions with nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: They are both wheelchair dependent in their golden years and Mdm Auo is also living with dementia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the therapeutic garden, they enjoy hands-on gardening activities amidst nature and explore sensory plants, like pandan, which evokes memories of local culinary delights.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We now have 17 therapeutic gardens within our parks island-wide, which is more than halfway to our target of having 30 by 2030.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, as we expand our network of parks in the coming years, we will incorporate more therapeutic landscapes and pro-health features where feasible, such as the upcoming Teachers' Estate Park and the park at Spottiswoode.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also ensuring our parks and gardens are accessible for a diverse range of users, including seniors, children with special needs and wheelchair users, so as to facilitate interactions with nature and encourage active living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, in East Coast Park, the KPMG Wellness Garden incorporates barrier-free paths and features a wheelchair-friendly trampoline and accessible lookout platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For our Nature Parks, Rifle Range Nature Park also features a wheelchair-friendly boardwalk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Last year, we reopened Sisters' Islands Marine Park, which offers barrier-free amenities, including a floating boardwalk, which doubles as a coral habitat and research site.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Residents can also look forward to a wheelchair-accessible jetty at Pulau Ubin, which will commence work this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap and Mr Dennis Tan asked about the lift provision in our HDB estates and improving accessibility for residents facing mobility challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I fully appreciate the points raised by Members and can empathise with the difficulties that mobility challenged residents face.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Since January 2023, we have offered LUP to 28 HDB blocks that do not have direct lift access.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: HDB is constantly studying how to make our blocks more accessible and inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It keeps abreast of technological development and trials potential solutions to determine their feasibility and cost-effectiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Over the years, HDB has explored mechanical solutions, such as chairlifts and stair climbers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, these were not implemented due to safety concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: HDB will continue to explore new ways to bring direct lift access to the remaining blocks, such as working with research institutes to better leverage technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As HDB does so, it has put in place measures to support households that face mobility challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, these households can tap on the Lift access Housing Grant (LHG), which can support successful applicants with up to $30,000 to buy new and resale HDB flats that have direct lift access.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This grant is intended to assist households that require direct lift access due to mobility challenges in securing homes that are more accessible and convenient for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I encourage households with pressing accessibility needs to approach HDB for assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Members can also direct these households that require such assistance to our HDB colleagues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: HDB will seek to understand the circumstances of the household and provide the necessary support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In response to Mr Faisal Manap's query on LUP for the three blocks, the current lift configurations were decided in consultation with residents and their representatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: They meet the objective of achieving direct lift access for every resident and were also successfully polled by the residents of the block.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin, Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Henry Kwek asked about how we can empower more people to be involved in our City in Nature journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We work closely with the community, industry partners and stakeholders to realise our City in Nature vision and we are very grateful for their support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We encourage interested residents to step forward and work alongside us in stewarding our City in Nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: When we embark on new park projects, we also involve residents in designing features that will cater to their needs and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Interested residents can also be involved in safeguarding biodiversity, such as through the 100k Corals Initiative, which Ms Nadia has also asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have begun working with experts to develop a coral reef restoration plan, which will guide future restoration efforts and plan to involve the wider community in our efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also very encouraged to see residents initiating green efforts to enliven shared spaces, as Ms Carrie Tan has mentioned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Through the Lively Places Fund (LPF), we have supported ground-up efforts, including allotment or community gardens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To make it easier for communities to set up gardens in their estates, we have simplified the LPF application process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Going forward, communities will be able to submit proposals for gardening initiatives, including on top of underutilised HDB multi-storey carparks via a centralised application portal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Applications will open every six months and more details will be shared by HDB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Besides gardening, LPF supports community-driven projects that transform public spaces into active, vibrant spaces that bring communities together and we welcome such applications via the same portal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The community also plays a key role in safeguarding animal health and welfare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In light of the cases of animal cruelty and neglect we have encountered in the past year, we have been hearing greater calls to review our penalties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked for an update on our ongoing review of the Animals and Birds Act (ABA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The ABA provides us with the powers to detect, prevent and control the spread of animal diseases and to safeguard animal welfare in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are reviewing the regulatory framework for the prevention and control of animal diseases and veterinary health products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This includes measures to stem animal smuggling and ensure the quality of veterinary health products (VHPs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also reviewing enforcement powers and regulatory levers for animal welfare and management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, we are reviewing the licensing regime for regulated pet sector activities and penalties for animal cruelty offences, including the disqualification order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: NParks has been conducting small-group discussions with the relevant stakeholders and incorporating their inputs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We intend to share more details later this year and will conduct consultations with a broader set of stakeholders to get feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Last year, we launched the Cat Management Framework to enhance the welfare and traceability of cats, which includes the licensing of pet cats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the sterilisation for pet cats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have just started implementing the cat management framework, which requires extensive effort on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For now, we will monitor the situation and work closely with our partners to raise awareness on the benefits of sterilisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin, Mr Chong Kee Hiong, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about our wildlife management approach, including our pest bird management efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To ensure public health and safety, we will continue to work closely with relevant agencies and stakeholders on our science and community-based approach to manage wildlife populations and strengthen awareness on managing human-wildlife encounters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have stepped up efforts to manage our pest bird populations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In an effort to stem the growth of the crow population and reduce the risk to public safety, NParks has since last year progressively taken on the function of removing crow nests in trees within areas managed by Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To address the bird feeding situation, we partnered Town Councils and agencies last year to deploy more CCTV cameras and enforcement personnel at identified feeding hotspots.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Last year, we took action against 258 incidents for feeding pigeons illegally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For feeders with mental health needs, NParks works with agencies to understand their motivations, address misconceptions and discourage them from feeding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will continue to collaborate with Active Ageing Centres to raise awareness among the elderly on the negative impacts of bird feeding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To complement these efforts, we have also ramped up education and outreach on bird feeding and food waste management at food and bin centres, in collaboration with NEA and SFA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Chairman, please allow me say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These gardens are thoughtfully designed to cater to a diverse range of users, including seniors, children with special needs and wheelchair users, to facilitate interactions with nature, improve well-being and encourage active living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Singaporeans can look forward to more green spaces that incorporate therapeutic landscapes and pro-health features, such as the upcoming gardens in Teachers' Estate Park and park at Spottiswoode. : Sir, please let me conclude.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As Singapore continues to develop, we will ensure that all Singaporeans feel fulfilled, included and empowered in their communities and homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are heartened to see community stewardship for our estates, animals and nature, and we will keep working closely with our residents as we push forward with our efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Together, we can nurture a Singapore that is vibrant and inclusive for many generations to come.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over the years, the Government has uplifted families in need through targeted and progressive shifts in our public housing policy.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, I will share more about how we will strengthen our support for the vulnerable to achieve two objectives: stability and empowerment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Public Rental Scheme has been a social safety net for our lower-income and vulnerable households, providing them a stable home as they navigate other life challenges.
