speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: During COVID-19, applications for rental flats surged and waiting times increased to up to 11 months.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are working to reduce waiting times further.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Second, to create a conducive living environment for our tenants to regain stability.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some may remember our older rental blocks, with long narrow corridors and units on both sides, and often clustered together.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We no longer build rental housing that way.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, rental blocks are interspersed with sold blocks and built with similar designs as sold blocks.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Going a step further, we have been building rental flats in the same blocks as sold flats, to encourage social mixing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To better meet the needs of our tenants, we have also been adjusting rental flat designs, such as building new rental flats with high partitions to provide more privacy for tenants under the Joint Singles Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, we piloted the Single Room Shared Facilities model to provide single tenants with their own room, while sharing common facilities like toilets and kitchens.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Tenants have moved in from August last year and many were pleased to have their own room.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to learn from this pilot and improve the experience for our single tenants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are committed to supporting all public rental households on their home ownership journey, starting with families with children or ComLink+ families.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many of these families face complex and overlapping challenges, such as balancing employment and childcare responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Take Mdm Christabel Tan, for example, one of our public rental tenants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After her husband's passing, she became the sole breadwinner of the family, raising three young children on her own.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: She took on a part-time job, so she could still take care of her children when she was not working.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: However, with her limited bandwidth and unstable income, home ownership seemed out of reach and she applied for a rental flat instead.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have taken steps to better support families like Mdm Tan.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since late last year, HDB provides proactive home ownership guidance to ComLink+ families upon their entry to public rental.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When Mdm Tan recently collected the keys to her rental flat, an HDB officer spoke with her to understand her home ownership aspirations, work out her housing budget with her based on the housing grants and loan she is eligible for and provide tailored advice on her housing options.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: She was very thankful for the personalised guidance from HDB.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It gave her clarity that a stable income with CPF contribution is crucial for her to build up her savings and close the $30,000 shortfall to buy a 3-room flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To her, home ownership is no longer a distant dream, but an attainable goal.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also do more to support families like Mdm Tan who need help to bridge the last mile towards home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, the Fresh Start Housing Scheme (Fresh Start) provides holistic support for second-timer public rental families with children to be proud home owners again.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Another 28 families have booked their flat and are waiting for their keys.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will do more to support more families to realise their home ownership aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As the Prime Minister had announced in his Budget Statement, we will be enhancing Fresh Start to support more ComLink+ families in public rental on their home ownership journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will benefit first-timer families, like Mdm Tan, who find it challenging to buy a 99-year lease flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With this change, she will be able to afford a shorter-lease 3-room Standard flat and achieve her goal of owning a flat sooner.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Like all other first-timers, they will continue to benefit from the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG) of up to $120,000, in lieu of the Fresh Start Housing Grant.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Next, we will increase the Fresh Start Housing Grant for second-timer ComLink+ families in public rental from $50,000 to $75,000.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With this enhancement, eligible families will receive an upfront disbursement of $60,000 into their CPF Ordinary Account before key collection, to help defray immediate costs of buying a home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The remaining $15,000 will be disbursed in equal tranches over five years after key collection to help families manage their mortgage payments.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Eligible families can look forward to tapping on the increased grant from the July 2025 sales exercise.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I recently visited one of our Fresh Start families, Mdm Nureezan and her two young daughters, Azura and Adiera, at their new flat in Marsiling.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When Mdm Nureezan was living in a rental flat, people told her that she would never be able to own a home of her own as a divorced, single parent.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Knowing the importance for her children to have a better living environment, she was determined to buy her own flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Fresh Start made home ownership possible for Mdm Nureezan.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With the Fresh Start Housing Grant, she was able to buy a new 2-room Sales of Balance flat with a 55-year lease, that is fortunately near her workplace and children’s school.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: She also benefitted from priority allocation under the Tenants’ Priority Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Her family moved into their new flat within a year, with minimal renovations needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Her journey was not easy, but she persevered and worked hard for her daughters.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: She told me that her daughters were overjoyed with tears on the day of moving into their new flat and said this to her “Mama, you made our dream come true.” Truly, home ownership is a dream for many.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are encouraged by this, and will continue working with our social agencies and community partners to enable more to do the same.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Home ownership is a journey, not a destination.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It comes with many responsibilities and requires careful financial planning.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As our tenants take this important step, we will continue to guide and support them every step of the way.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Chairman, allow me to now speak in Malay. :   Home ownership represents a significant milestone for many people.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are committed to supporting all public rental households to own their homes, starting with families with children, or ComLink+ families.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When families collect the keys to their rental flat, HDB officers will guide them on their home ownership journey – the HDB officers will engage them to understand the families’ aspirations, assess their financial situation, and provide tailored advice on their housing options We will also do more to support families who may need help to bridge the last mile towards home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, the Fresh Start Housing Scheme provides holistic support to help second-timer public rental families with children to be home owners again.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As announced by the Prime Minister in his Budget Statement, we will be enhancing the Fresh Start Housing Scheme to support more ComLink+ families in public rental on their home ownership journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Like all other first-timers, they will continue to benefit from the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant of up to $120,000, in lieu of the Fresh Start Housing Grant.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First-timer families who are eligible can apply for the Fresh Start Housing Scheme from April this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Eligible families can look forward to tapping on the increased grant from the July 2025 sales exercise. : Sir, let me conclude by re-affirming our commitment to uplifting those in need, providing them with stability and empowering them to lead lives of dignity and opportunity.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To make a lasting impact, we need the support from every member of the society, including all of us here in this House.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together, we can build a stronger, more inclusive community, so that Singapore remains a home that all Singaporeans are proud of.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Before I go to clarifications, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, you have a clarification to make?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And the reasons are as what I have stated in the speech.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have to finish at the guillotine time of 1.50 pm I see a number of hands, so my first request to all is to keep your clarifications short.

speaker: The Chairman
text: And likewise for the responses from the front bench, to also keep it short.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I have a clarification for Minister Desmond Lee.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Beyond the Home Improvement Programme, does the Government have other plans around rejuvenation for Singapore on a broader level?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Just confirm, the Member is asking about HDB or generally?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chairman, I had spoken earlier in my speech about HIP, which is about making improvements within the home, resolving common maintenance issues in the home, and I have also spoken about EASE to make our homes in our HDB estate safer for seniors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It probably may be better characterised as a very significant NRP.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NRP is about specific neighbourhoods but revitalising our heartlands, the ROH, allows us to look at the entire estate, the town centre, the neighbourhoods, the precincts, and to make improvements across large parts of the town.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, those are with regard to improving the livability and the quality of life in public housing estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chairman, I had also spoken about how we are making efforts to also improve our private housing estates, particularly for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We see as we go around the private housing estates, whether it is a group of condominiums or landed estates, there are seniors living there, and sometimes they face challenges too in getting about daily life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And so, the Estate Upgrading Programme (EUP) has been around for some time, the different tranches to enable us to work with communities to improve the liveability of those private estates – for example, covering drains, improving walkways, improving pocket greens and parks for inter-generational bonding, for instance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we also had a mirror to what in HDB we call the Silver Upgrading Programme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And the Member might have heard about the Silver Upgrading Programme, which is a kind of NRP, but it covers estates which had already gone through upgrading before, through the MUP, for instance; but with many seniors, we come back again and look specifically at what needs to be done to improve the public housing estates for seniors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, the mirror on the private housing estate side is EUP Silver.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: EUP is across the board, but EUP Silver allows us to zoom in specifically on the needs of the elderly living in the private estates as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, these are, in sum, a range of programmes that allow us to improve the livability of our estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And you heard just now Senior Minister of State Sim Ann talk about the Community Improvement Programme Committee (CIPC) that allows us to make year-on-year, smaller scale improvements to improve the quality of life as well.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And thank you to the MND office holders for responding to the cuts.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: First on Minister Lee's speech, the Minister spoke about a number of new initiatives, new scanning technology for flats which have a persistent facade-related leakages.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just some clarity on that pilot, whether it covers a specific cluster or Town Council, or is it more general to some of the more problematic flats, and whether other Town Councils can request for the extension of this technology to persistent facade-related problems for flats in their Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Minister referred to the Silver Housing slew of policies that MND has and how those are going to be improved.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I would just seek clarification on the Community Care Apartments.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: There was an announcement, I believe sometime in late 2023, about the total number of Community Care Apartments that were being earmarked for construction until the end of the decade.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My final clarification for the Minister pertains to a point I made in my Budget debate speech with regard to the number of ultimate dwelling units that were reflected in the HDB Annual Report in the year 2019-2020 and how that number increased in the latest HDB Annual Report.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: If the Minister does not have the reply, I can always file a Parliamentary Question for that clarification.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: He can just let me know whether I need to do that.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: With Aljunied Hougang Town Council having received little to no CIPC funding from 2011 to 2021, one can understand why this source of funding is important for Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I appreciate the funding that has been extended after 2021 and I note Senior Minister of State's reply in terms of how MND will look at some of the projects that have been put up.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: For Aljunied Hougang Town Council, we will put up projects subsequently with a focus on recreational upgrades and upgrades for seniors in our town, because it is a more mature town.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, just to record my appreciation for that reply.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have enterprises that are experimenting with ways to better scan the walls and ceilings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Because visual inspection can go so far, but if you are able to look beneath the surface, you might be able to better pinpoint the source of leaks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are going to select the flats that will allow us to test out the efficacy of this technology.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And if it is successful, then we will try to expand it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said earlier, Mr Chairman, we will look to strengthen capabilities across our Town Councils, as well as our BE sector, our contractors and all who will need to be able to know how to use this technology and to be able to make more durable repairs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The third question, I must apologise to the Leader of Opposition.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I might have missed that in the Budget.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Maybe I will just invite him to file a Written Question and I will then have a look at the issue.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first one for Senior Minister of State Sim Ann.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How will MND ensure that the expansion of the Budget Meal Initiative is sustainable for operators and individual stall owners?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second clarification is for Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How, in his speech, he mentioned that MND has exceeded their target of developing 130 hectares of new parks by 2026, and have made good progress in restoring habitats and establishing park connectors.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Does NParks intend to review the next bound of these targets?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We take in feedback from the operators with regards to the implementation of the budget meals.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is one way in which we check that the scheme is sustainable.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And as I have also shared in the speech, we are going beyond that to review the PQM framework, as well as considering measures to deter overly high bids, because we are mindful about the possible impact on stall holders who may feel squeezed by providing budget meals on the one hand, but they may possibly also face the requirement for high stall rents.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I think in putting in place these measures, we can assure stall holders that we do have the sustainability of their livelihoods at heart.

speaker: The Chairman
text: My apologies, I think that Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How wanted to respond to the earlier clarification?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Joan Pereira, I will call you on again.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We announced our vision to transform Singapore from a City in a Garden to a City in Nature at COS 2020.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We were still in the midst of COVID-19 half a decade ago.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We shared our aspiration for Singaporeans to co-exist with flora and fauna, and talked about the importance of enhancing greenery across our island in the face of climate change, more extreme weather conditions and also increased urbanisation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And we are very heartened to see that we are making steady and strong progress in meeting many of these targets, even at the halfway point.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And many of these targets span the four key areas of our City in Nature vision, namely: first, conserving and extending our natural capital; second, intensifying nature in our parks and gardens; third, to restore nature in our urban landscape; and fourth, strengthening connectivity between our green spaces.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, we have made good progress over the last few years, notwithstanding many of challenges of COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We are now, as Mr Chong pointed out, at the midway mark.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We will take stock of our progress and more importantly, identify the areas where we can strengthen our efforts, where needed, to make greater strides to meeting our targets.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I just want to make a final point to say that, ultimately, these are targets, but it is really the spirit of it.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is our commitment to shaping a City in Nature and we must take ambitious steps to weave nature more closely as part of our urban environment, especially as a small and densely populated city-state, with very tight land use constraints.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is a major endeavour that the Government cannot undertake alone.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We will need the support of the community and as mentioned earlier in my COS speech, I encourage many more Singaporeans, like-minded Singaporeans, enterprises, corporates, community partners, to work together with us on this important effort.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We still have many clarifications, but we only have 15 minutes left.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: I have got two clarifications for Minister Lee.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: On the scanning technology that the Leader of Opposition also asked about, that would be piloted in 70 units, can I make a request to have my Henderson Crescent flats be part of the pilot, if it is not already in the list?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The second clarification, our seniors' needs are becoming more diverse.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The Minister has briefly touched on how the Government intends to support our seniors' housing and retirement needs beyond these measures that were shared.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Can the Minister elaborate on other efforts by the Government to meet our seniors' evolving housing needs?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To reply to the first question, let HDB identify the flats which would best allow them to test out the technology.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have been doing a lot of the work in Building Research Institute (BRI), which is HDB's research institute.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want to be able to try this out in more realistic settings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we certainly will bear the Member's offer in mind and look forward to her support if there are any units in her area.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The other question is about how we can better support seniors' housing and retirement needs, am I right?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have earlier spoken about various upgrading programmes, to make our homes and our neighbourhoods safer and more senior-friendly, so that is one.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In terms of housing options, when it comes to HDB housing, seniors have a whole range of monetisation options, as I mentioned earlier in my speech.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are also, of course, Community Care Apartments that our seniors can look to move to.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a concept where housing and social and care come together in the estate to allow our seniors to age within the community more effectively.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, these are the things that we have been doing to better support our seniors with a wider range of housing options, through a suite of monetisation options and to better support our seniors, for example, through SHB as they seek to right-size.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I am giving priority to those who filed more cuts.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Chairman, I would like to ask MND two clarifications for the BE sector.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: First of all, some consultants are concerned about being held responsible for what you call excessive contractual liabilities arising from projects and project disputes.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Can he share how the proposed review of public sector procurement practices could help alleviate that?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Second is more on the BETC grants, which will go very far to help the sector.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Can MND share more about how, specifically, it will help the BE sector, which is essential for MND's construction plans for the future?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Chairman, before I respond to those clarifications, I just need to make one small correction with regard to my speech, where I had earlier said that the date of when Mr Muhammad Khalil had started his career as a draughtsman in 2025.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Coming to the clarifications as sought by Mr Henry Kwek.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the first one about the consultants being responsible for contractual liabilities, the task force acknowledges the industry's concerns about the balance of risk between service buyers and the BE consultants, and how being held responsible for excessive liabilities may impact the consultant's business sustainability.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For service buyers, having their consultants sufficiently insured by PII would give assurance on the consultant's ability to compensate them should there be a need to do so.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And at the sectoral level, having sufficient PII coverage will also allow for more efficient risk sharing, thereby strengthening the sustainability of our BE professions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, it supports enhancement of enterprise capabilities, such as in adopting lean construction practices and collaborative contracting.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Second, it will support adoption of advanced technologies, including robotics and automation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Third, it supports the building of firms' manpower capabilities, such as in innovative sourcing methods, job redesign and specialised training.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We are open to considering other relevant initiatives that align with the ITM and which would contribute to the sector's overall transformation.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: First, on my suggestion for a separate buyer stamp duty regime for the HDB market to give the Government greater policy optionality to cool the resale market quickly when needed, I would just like to ask the Minister if the Ministry would be minded to consider that suggestion, and if not, why not?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The second question is to Senior Minister of State Tan, and it is about pest birds.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I just want to stress again that this can be a huge pain point for us locally, especially when the bird population flares up and we need quick fixes to bring down the bird population.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: So, really, are there further strategies and measures that the authorities are considering to help the Town Councils to manage this problem?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And could he also share further details about the pilot Pigeon Management Framework that he mentioned in his reply?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Principally, firstly, we have to make sure that the property market, whether it is on the HDB side or the private housing side, is in line with economic fundamentals.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We need to understand the causes of market movements and then target measures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That means you inject supply to meet demand.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: You inject supply in order to assure people that there is available units coming on stream.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And then, there are demand side measures, for example, tightening on loans, limiting eligibility, which can sometimes be painful as we have seen, and these are demand side measures, and you need to allow them to work through the market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we certainly will consider all suggestions that both he and other Members may have given.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Indeed, for many town councils across the board, managing pest birds is something that they are working on and we see the number of feedback and complaints coming up, rising over the years.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The Member mentioned pest birds but maybe allow me to just speak about two specific species because there are slightly different techniques and approach that we use for pigeons as well as crows.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Basically, there are roughly, broadly, about four pest bird species in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We have feral pigeons, common and white-minted mynahs and house crows.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, most of the feedback is really around pigeons and crows.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is something that the HDB has been working very closely with Town Councils to manage some of these disamenities and to manage the population issues on the ground.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Minister of State Tan, I hope you can make it short.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I am trying to squeeze one more clarification.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The Member asked about the pilot that we are working on with three Town Councils (TCs).

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I mentioned earlier Bishan-Toa Payoh, Ang Mo Kio and Tanjong Pagar.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is not just about reducing the population sizes of the pigeons in the estate, but it is really to minimise the food sources which is one important driver for the pigeon population.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, the Member asked what they can do or how can they work more closely with different agencies.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The first will be making sure that food sources can be minimised.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For example, also, working together with NEA to monitor waste disposal activities near bulk bins and for the Town Councils to also take enforcement action against improper refuse disposal.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On the second species of pest bird issues is really around crows, and that is where NParks has leaned in, leaned forward to work closely with Town Councils to minimise the crow issues on the ground.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, there are things that we can do, sensible things we can do.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: There are a number of things we can do as well in terms of habitant modification.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The Town Councils can work together with NParks to step up pruning of the trees in hotspot to discourage roosting and we can also improve trapping efficacy; for example, through the use of new designs and trapping methods such as mist nets.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And thirdly, again, similar to the pigeon issue is about food reduction so I look forward to Town Councils working together of NParks to minimise the availability of food sources and to work together with agencies, like NEA and SFA, to improve food and refuse disposal.
